title: Characterization of encoded reachability
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean string, and let $s,u$ be natural numbers. The code $u$ is reachable from the initial configuration code by zero or more encoded steps in which both configurations lie in the $s$-window if and only if there is a finite Boolean choice string $w$ such that every configuration along the run determined by each prefix of $w$ lies in the $s$-window, and the code of the final configuration is $u$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet
